text:
Maria (Finance): Heads up — we just received a late vendor invoice that pushes ~48.2k of usage into March. This will affect the March revenue schedule/deferral. Need quick decision: record as a March prior-period adjustment or put it through as an April accrual? cc @Jon (RevenueOps) @Devon (Billing) @sam (Audit)

bot-invoices: New invoice #489201 received: https://invoices.redwood.local/489201. Invoice date: 2026-03-25. Service period: 2026-03-01 to 2026-03-31. Amount: $48,245.12. Attached: scanned_PDF (pdf).

Devon (Billing): Pulled the billing run — ETL lag caused the usage to land late. CSV extract (first 3 rows):
```
customer_id,usage_date,tokens,amount
ACME-001,2026-03-28,1_240_000,1200.00
NIMBUS-12,2026-03-30,5_600_000,5400.00
SPROUT-7,2026-03-31,18_000_000,41645.12
```
Looks like one large account plus misc. No duplicates in ledger.

Jon (RevenueOps): Given materiality and audit trail, I propose a March prior-period adjustment so revenue is matched to service period. Suggested JE (to be reviewed by Audit):
```
Date: 2026-03-31
Dr Accounts Receivable 48,245.12
  Cr Deferred Revenue 48,245.12
(Record vendor-billed usage into March deferral schedule; will amortize per existing schedule)
```
This keeps the P&L timing consistent with service. We'll also update the revenue schedule meta pointing to invoice 489201.

sam (Audit): +1 to prior-period adjustment. Please include: 1) rationale memo, 2) evidence of invoice/service period, 3) sign-offs. Tag the JE as "post-close prior period" and include original scanned invoice. Also confirm impact on ARR/quarter metrics — seems limited but call out in memo.

Leigh (Sales Ops): One more wrinkle — this vendor invoice triggers a retro credit from the pricing experiment for SPROUT-7 (~$5k) that we need to apply to the customer's account. We generally prefer to apply credits on the next invoice (April) for customer experience. If we book the full amount into March, how do we reflect the pending credit?

Devon (Billing): We can net the credit against AR in March or show a separate liability (Customer Credits). Suggested netting JE if we want clean AR:
```
Date: 2026-03-31
Dr Accounts Receivable 48,245.12
  Cr Deferred Revenue 43,245.12
  Cr Customer Credit Liability 5,000.00
(Record gross invoice into deferral schedule and set aside credit liability for retro pricing experiment)
```
If we instead want the customer-facing credit to hit April, keep the credit liability and reduce AR only when we issue the credit on April invoice.

Maria (Finance): Good options. Audit preference is prior-period adj, and Sales prefers credit applied in April. I recommend we book the gross into March deferrals and record a Customer Credit Liability for $5k. That keeps March revenue matching service, and the customer credit is tracked separately until applied. I'll draft the memo and tag everyone for approval.

Jon (RevenueOps): I'll update the revenue schedule to include the gross invoice and add a line to amortize per the usage schedule. Also will mark the affected accounts so Optimize knows not to re-suggest quota/quant settings for that run.

sam (Audit): Approve the approach (gross into March + customer credit liability). Please route the memo to audit@redwood.com and include the invoice PDF and the billing CSV extract.

Devon (Billing): Once memo is approved, I'll prepare the JE for posting and attach supporting docs. Will also create the April credit memo for SPROUT-7 so Sales can confirm customer communication.

Maria (Finance): Thanks — action items: 1) I will write the memo and circulate for approvals (target: EOD today), 2) @Devon to prepare JE after approvals, 3) @Jon to update rev schedule, 4) @Leigh to confirm credit comms for April.

Jon (RevenueOps): :thumbsup: I'll also update the close checklist to flag delayed-usage invoices so we can catch these earlier.

sam (Audit): Approved. Send the memo to me and cc financials.

Maria (Finance): Great — moving to action. I'll post the memo link here when done and mark this thread closed. Thanks everyone.
